title.zh: 只剩诗这一处：胡适怎样把争论变成《尝试集》
title.en: Only Poetry Was Left: How an Argument Turned into Hu Shi's Book of Experiments

dek.zh: 1915到1917年，一个自称保守、认为语言文字最不易变的中国留学生，按他自述，是被几首打油诗和朋友的反对，一步步推到只用白话作诗的决定上；更早，一张传单让他起意在文字改革上尽点力。他把主张写得温和，《新青年》主编陈独秀却替他把旗子举高成“革命”。
dek.en: Between 1915 and 1917, a Chinese student in America who called himself a conservative — who thought language and writing the world's most unchanging things — was, by his own account, pushed by a few doggerel verses and his friends' opposition into writing poetry in the spoken language alone; earlier, a leaflet had first moved him to want to do something about reforming the written language. He worded his claim modestly; Chen Duxiu, editor of New Youth, raised the banner for him, into "revolution."

paras.zh: 一群在美国读书的中国朋友，为中国文学该怎样改革争论了一年多。1916年7月，湖上一场几乎翻船的风雨，和一位朋友用老字写成的纪事诗，又掀起一轮新的争吵，争论最后收缩到一个问题上：诗能不能用白话写。站在一边的是胡适，而他一向说自己是保守的人，认为语言文字是世界上最保守的东西，比宗教还保守，还说自己这一路是被「逼上梁山」的。这句成语说的是一个人为环境所迫，不得已而做出违反他本意的非常行为。
paras.en: A group of Chinese friends studying in America argued for more than a year over how Chinese literature should change. In July 1916 a storm on a lake that nearly capsized their boat, and a friend's poem about it written in archaic words, set off a fresh round of quarrelling, and the dispute finally narrowed to one question: could poetry be written in baihua, the everyday spoken language? On one side stood Hu Shi, who called himself a conservative: language and writing, he liked to say, are the most conservative things in the world, more conservative than religion. He also said he had been pushed down this road: bi shang Liangshan, driven to Liangshan, an idiom for someone forced by circumstances into extraordinary acts against his own intentions.

paras.zh: 反对他的主要是两位朋友：一位是去哈佛升学、最坚定的反对者梅光迪，另一位是同在康乃尔、写诗嘲笑过他的任鸿隽。争的是白话能不能用来写文学。到1916年夏天，朋友们已承认白话可以写小说、演说，唯独不肯承认它能作诗，反对者已经退到只剩一处：诗。按胡适的说法，难处在于从来没有中国作家认真着实用白话作诗，他在中国诗词中能找到的白话诗只有一首，甚至只是一首中的几句。按他自己的说法，这许多严肃的讨论都只源于一首送别诗引起的小小偶然事件；让他下定决心不写旧诗、要写就用活的语言来写的，则是又一件偶然发生的小事——湖上那场险事。
paras.en: His chief opponents were two friends: Mei Guangdi, bound for Harvard and his most determined opponent, and Ren Hongjun, also at Cornell, who had mocked him in verse. The quarrel was over whether the vernacular could serve literature. By the summer of 1916 his friends granted that it would do for fiction and speeches, but not for poetry. Poetry was the last fortress. The difficulty, as Hu saw it, was that no Chinese writer had ever seriously written poetry in the vernacular; in all of Chinese verse he could find only one such poem, perhaps only a few lines of one. In his own telling, all the serious discussion grew out of a small accident set off by a farewell poem; what made him resolve to stop writing old-style verse and write only in the living language was another small accident, the incident on the lake.

paras.zh: 更早还有一段引子。一位热心改革的书记，总在留学生每月的奖学金支票信封里夹寄小传单，其中一条是「废除汉字，改用字母！」。约在1915年（胡适说“我想是”），胡适回了一张很不客气的字条，叫他「最好闭起鸟嘴！」
paras.en: There was an earlier prelude. A clerk keen on reform used to slip leaflets into the envelopes that carried the students' monthly scholarship checks; one slogan, in translation, was to abolish the Chinese characters and switch to an alphabet. Around 1915 (Hu said he thought it was then), Hu wrote back a rude little note telling the man, in translation, that he had better shut his beak.

paras.zh: 字条寄出后他心中懊悔，觉得不该对一位和善又有心改革的人如此不礼貌。他还想到：假如这样的人不够资格谈这个问题，那么够资格的人实在更该认真研究。于是他和一位同学商定，在留学生会的年会上各写一篇论文讨论中国文字问题，他自己的题目是怎样使文言易于教授。
paras.en: Once the note was sent he regretted it: the man was kind and sincere about reform, and the rudeness was uncalled for. Then a further thought: if men like him were not qualified to discuss the question, the qualified should do the work. So he agreed with a fellow student that each would write a paper on the problem of the Chinese script for the annual meeting of a Chinese students' association. Hu's topic was how to make the classical written language easier to teach.

paras.zh: 在那篇论文里，他提出文言是「半死的语言」。理由很具体：有些词还活着，有些已经死了——“狗”字今天仍在用，“犬”字就不用了；“骑马”仍是日常用语，“乘马”事实上已不通行。所以教活的语言和教半死的语言，方法应该大不相同。他晚年回忆说，自己后来“白话是活的语言、文言半死”的主张，就是从这个时期开始的。
paras.en: Hu's paper called the classical written language — in our translation — a half-dead language. Some words live, some have died: gou, "dog," is still in use; quan, the old word for the same animal, is not. "Ride a horse" is everyday speech; the classical equivalent is a dead phrase. So the teaching of a living language and of a half-dead one must be very different business. Looking back, he said his doctrine — vernacular alive, classical half-dead — had begun in this period.

heading.en: A Year and More of Argument

paras.zh: 争论是从一首送别诗开始的。胡适准备离开康乃尔时，梅光迪正要去哈佛升学。胡适写了首相当长的打油诗为他送行，里面塞进十一个外国人的名字。同在康乃尔的任鸿隽把这些名字连缀起来，作诗嘲笑他「文学今革命，作诗送胡生！」。胡适自认那首送行诗立意严肃：诗里鼓励朋友们留意今后中国文学的发展，并说致力于中国文学革命，贡献不下于征服自然，他叫它作「缩地戡天」。所以他不肯轻轻放过，在去纽约的火车上作了答诗，第一次写下“诗国革命”的念头：「诗国革命何自始？要须作诗如作文！」
paras.en: It began with a farewell poem. When Hu was preparing to leave Cornell, Mei Guangdi was about to go on to Harvard. Hu sent him off with a doggerel poem, long by Chinese standards, stuffed with eleven foreign names. Ren Hongjun, also at Cornell, strung the names into a mock verse of his own, which in our translation runs: literature's revolution today, a poem to send off Hu. Hu would not let it pass. His send-off had been meant in earnest. It urged his friends to watch where Chinese literature went next, and it ranked a revolution in Chinese literature with conquering nature, which he called, in our translation, shrinking the earth and taming the heavens. So on the train to New York he wrote an answer, and in it first set down the idea of a revolution in the poetry world. His couplet, in our translation, asks where that revolution should begin, and answers that poetry must be written like prose.

paras.zh: 这句“作诗如作文”引来一场是非。梅、任都参战，梅光迪认为诗之文字与文之文字自诗文以来（不论中西）早已分道而驰，根本不能混为一谈。辩论不休，牵涉愈多，内容愈复杂：用胡适自己的话说，朋友们愈辩愈保守，他也愈辩愈激进。
paras.en: Thus the slogan — write poetry like prose — started a fight. Mei and Ren both weighed in. Poetry and prose, Mei held, could never be mixed: poetic diction and prose diction had parted ways since each began, in China and the West alike. The debate never stopped, and the further it ran the more it dragged in. As Hu put it, the more his friends argued the more conservative they grew; the more he argued, the more radical.

paras.zh: 转机出现在1916年二三月。他形成一个概括观念：整部中国文学史就是一部文学工具变迁史，一个工具替代另一个工具；同时也是一部活文学逐渐代替死文学的历史。工具一旦活力消失、逐渐僵化，就要换一个，在这种嬗递中接受一个活的工具，他称之为“文学革命”。三月，他写长信给在哈佛的梅光迪，说中古以后老的语言工具已不够用，变迁在唐代便已发生：散文体裁发生革命，逐渐发展出以白话表达的语录体，先为和尚们采用，后来宋代哲学家用它记录哲学讨论，老百姓又用它作歌曲、编戏剧、写短篇和长篇小说。他说用白话写的活文学，最明显的如元曲，是民众不知不觉中完成的文学革命的最高潮，中国文学之复苏实得力于白话戏曲和白话小说之兴起。出乎他意料，这套由历史分析得出的结论，竟被这位保守朋友欣然接受。需要补一句：他们当时以为传统长篇小说都是元代作品，胡适本人晚年更正说，《水浒》一流的故事流传几百年，到明代才写成定稿。
paras.en: The turn came in February and March of 1916. Hu reached a general idea: the history of Chinese literature is a history of changing literary tools, one replacing another, and at the same time a history of living literature gradually displacing dead literature. When a tool loses its vitality and hardens it must be changed, and taking up a living tool in that succession is what he called literary revolution. In March he wrote a long letter to Mei, then at Harvard. After the medieval period, he wrote, the old language tool could no longer carry people's thoughts. The change had begun in the Tang, when prose style was revolutionized and a vernacular recorded-sayings style grew up. Monks took it up first, then Song philosophers used it for their discussions, and then ordinary people used it for songs, plays, stories and novels. Vernacular literature of that kind, Yuan drama most obviously, was, he said, the climax of a literary revolution the masses completed without knowing it; the revival of Chinese literature owed much to the rise of vernacular drama and fiction. To Hu's surprise, this conclusion drawn from historical analysis was gladly accepted by his conservative friend. One note: they then took the great traditional novels for Yuan works. Hu corrected himself in later years, saying that stories like Water Margin circulated for centuries before being written down in final form under the Ming.

paras.zh: 1916年7月6日，他在日记里写下九条主张，头两条是「今日之文言乃是一种半死的文字。」和「今日之白话是一种活的语言。」他说这九条很确切地表达了他策动中国文学革命的中心思想；又说这许多严肃的讨论和历史性的研析，其实都只源于一首送别诗引起的小小偶然事件。
paras.en: Then the diary. On July 6, 1916, he set down nine propositions; the first two, in translation: the classical written language of today is a half-dead form of writing; the vernacular of today is a living language. These nine, he said, expressed precisely the central ideas behind his launching of China's literary revolution — and all these serious discussions and historical analyses came out of one small accident, a farewell poem to a friend going to Harvard.

paras.zh: 两天之后，湖上出了桩险事。7月8日，任鸿隽、梅光迪等几位朋友在凯约嘉湖上划船，片云头上黑，忽然刮起风暴，雨落下来。他们急忙往岸边划，几乎把船弄翻，个个淋得狼狈不堪。对这批中国留学生来说，这也算件险事。任鸿隽随后写了一首四言古诗《泛湖即事》附在信里，请胡适批评。诗中用了《诗经》里“言”字一类的老字，而胡适此前恰好写过一篇《言字解》。他不喜欢这种陈腐文字与现代语言夹杂，回信说此诗不好，因为「文字殊不调和」，又有「三千年前之死语」之说。任鸿隽不服，愤愤不平。更有意思的是梅光迪路见不平，写来一封十分激动的信反击。梅当时正受他那位保守派文学批评老师的影响，对胡适的一切激进主张都反对到底。他认为语言必须经过第一流的诗人加以锻炼，才能成为诗的语言；文学的文字，尤其是诗的文字，一定要由第一流的诗人和美术家加以美化，才能成为诗之文字。他据此对胡适的观念大加挞伐。
paras.en: Two days later came a close call on Cayuga Lake. On July 8 Ren Hongjun, Mei Guangdi and several other friends were rowing on the lake when a black cloud gathered overhead, a storm broke and the rain fell. Pulling for shore in a hurry they nearly capsized, and all came away soaked and dishevelled. For that band of Chinese students it was a real adventure, and Ren wrote it up in Fanhu jishi (Boating on the Lake), an old four-character-style poem he mailed to Hu for criticism. It used archaic words such as the particle yan, of the kind found in the Book of Songs. Hu had earlier written an essay on that very word, and he disliked dead diction mixed with modern language. He wrote back that the poem was bad because its wording was thoroughly incongruous, and he spoke of dead language of three thousand years ago (both paraphrased from the Chinese). Ren was indignant. More interesting was the letter that followed: Mei, riding to the rescue in high dudgeon. Mei was under the influence of his conservative teacher, a literary critic, and he opposed all of Hu's radicalism to the end. Language becomes poetic, he held, only after first-rate poets refine it, and the language of literature, poetry above all, must be beautified by first-rate poets and artists before it counts as poetic diction. On that ground he lashed Hu's ideas.

paras.zh: 胡适的回应是一首约一百句的滑稽打油诗，是他生平写的最长的一首。开头描写老梅大发脾气，再举许多例子开玩笑地驳“文字哪有死活”，并顺着对方的论点反将一军：文字须经诗人长期锻炼，这正是他想做的事，当代的诗人作家正该把这些俗语俗字锻炼起来，提高它们的地位，把它们提到诗歌文学里来。两位朋友读了大发雷霆，复信取笑他企图作白话诗。但胡适在信里发现两人有个共同的论调：白话的生动可以用在评话、故事、长篇小说等写作上，就是不能用在诗里。梅光迪排除得更多：在小说和民歌里白话可以用，但在高级散文里，肯定的是在诗里面，白话千万用不得。任鸿隽说得最干脆：「白话自有白话用处（如作小说、演说等），然不能用之于诗！」按胡适的归纳，朋友们在其他方面都已让步，只剩诗这一处还在争。
paras.en: Hu answered with a comic doggerel poem of about a hundred lines, the longest he ever wrote. It opened with Old Mei in a towering rage, piled up examples to mock the theory that words have no life or death, and turned Mei's own argument against him: if words must be forged by poets over long practice, that is exactly what he wanted. Contemporary poets and writers should take these vulgar, colloquial words, temper them, raise their standing and bring them into poetry. The burlesque threw both friends into a fury, and both wrote back to mock his attempt at vernacular verse. Yet Hu found a common line in their letters: the liveliness of the vernacular could serve storytelling, tales and novels, but not poetry. Mei excluded more: the vernacular was usable in fiction and folk songs, but in high prose, and certainly in poetry, it must never be used. Ren was bluntest; his letter said, in translation, that the vernacular has its own uses, such as novels and speeches, but cannot be used for poetry. As Hu summed it up, his friends had given way everywhere else; only poetry was still in dispute.

paras.zh: 于是问题收缩成一个点。胡适把反对理由排了队：第一，从来没有诗人用俗语俗字作过诗，他在中国诗词中只找到一首、甚至一首中的几句是白话，白话诗数量太少，这使朋友们振振有词；第二，也是朋友们更能言之成理的一条，从来没有中国作家认真着实用白话作诗，多半是兴之所至偶写几行，骨子里对白话有下意识的鄙弃。他的结论是：要说服朋友相信白话可以作诗，只有以身作则，认真尝试用白话作诗，除此之外没有别的办法。
paras.en: And so the dispute narrowed to a point: the vernacular for every department of literature except poetry. Hu ranked the objections. First, no poet had written in vulgar words and everyday speech — in Chinese poetry he could find one poem, perhaps a few lines of one; the scarcity of vernacular poems gave his friends their confident case. Second, and the more persuasive for his friends, no Chinese writer had seriously tried: a few vernacular lines in a fit of high spirits, no more, and beneath that a half-conscious contempt. To convince them there was one course only — set an example, seriously try to write vernacular poetry. Nothing else would do.

paras.zh: 七月底，他写信告诉这些朋友：白话也可以作诗，以往白话诗不多，今后可以多写，当务之急是自己认真着实地试验。七月二十六日他写信给任鸿隽，说「文字者，文学之器也」，文言决不足为吾国将来文学之利器，施耐庵、曹雪芹已经实地证明作小说之利器在于白话，「今尚需人实地试验白话是否可为韵文之利器耳」。他把这件事比作开辟新地：「我此时练习白话诗文，颇似新辟一文学殖民地」，可惜须单身匹马前往，难得同志结伴。信里也写到失败的可能：新开之地若尽是不毛之土，自己终归老于“文言诗国”也说不定；若侥幸有成，辟除荆棘之后自会开放门户，迎朋友同来。七月底八月初，他决定不再写旧诗词，专写白话诗，并在写出几首之前就给下一个诗集定名《尝试集》。
paras.en: In late July he wrote to these friends that the vernacular could be poetry: little had been written before, but more could be written now, in every colour and shape, and the urgent task was to experiment in earnest. On July 26 he wrote Ren — paraphrased here from the Chinese — that words are the instrument of literature, that the classical language could never be the sharp instrument China's future literature needed, and that Shi Nai'an and Cao Xueqin had proved in practice that the instrument for fiction is the vernacular; what remained was for someone to test in practice whether it could be the instrument of verse. He likened his practice in vernacular poetry and prose to opening up a new literary colony; it was a pity he had to go alone, with few companions. The letter also allowed for failure: if the new land proved to be sand and barren ground, he might end his days in the kingdom of classical poetry after all; if by luck he succeeded, after clearing the brambles he would open the gates and welcome his friends in. In late July and early August he decided to stop writing old-style verse — and before he had written more than a handful of vernacular poems, he had named the next collection Experiments.

paras.zh: 1916年十一月，他把一年多讨论的结果写成文章，提出八条很温和的建议，题目用的是“改良”和“刍议”。据他事后解释，“文学革命”一词在他自己的诗和信里、朋友给他的来信里早已常见，有时是开玩笑，有时也很严肃；但第一次把结论送到国内发表时，他考虑到老一辈保守分子无可怀疑的反对，刻意把文题写得温和而谦虚。文章誊了三份：一份交给他自己主编、当时由商务印书馆承印的《中国留美学生季报》，一份寄给陈独秀主编、已出版数年的《新青年》；陈独秀于1916年受聘为国立北京大学文科学长。
paras.en: In November 1916 he shaped more than a year of argument into an article with eight very moderate suggestions. Even the title was modest: he dropped "literary revolution," a phrase that had come up often in his own poems and letters and in his friends' letters to him, sometimes in jest and sometimes in earnest. This was the first time the conclusions would be sent home to China for publication. By his own later account, it was in view of the undoubted resistance of the older conservatives that he kept the wording gentle: reform, not revolution; a humble opinion, not dogma. He made three copies. One went to the Chinese Students' Quarterly he edited in America, then printed by the Commercial Press. Another went to New Youth, which Chen Duxiu, from 1916 dean of arts at National Peking University, had been editing for several years.

paras.zh: 1917年一月，文章在《新青年》刊出，文化界反应很大。北大有两位教授重视它。一位是陈独秀本人，本是死硬派的革命人物，随后写《文学革命论》响应，公开支持文学革命，并说首举义旗的是朋友胡适，自己高张大旗作声援。另一位是研究古典音韵学的教授，也是古文大家，他没有写文章，却写去小批评大捧场的长信，也在《新青年》发表，声势为之一振。胡适在康乃尔的同学、当年与他分写论文的赵元任，则常说胡适的白话诗文“不够白”，不是一般人常用的真正语体。胡适承认了，还打了个比方：像裹了四十年或者二十年小脚的女人，纵使把小脚放大，终究恢复不了天足。
paras.en: It appeared in New Youth in January 1917 and stirred a great response. Two Peking University professors took it seriously. One was Chen Duxiu himself, an unbending revolutionary. He answered with "On Literary Revolution," publicly backing a literary revolution and saying frankly that the banner had been raised by his friend Hu Shi; he himself was raising the banner high in his friend's support. The other, a professor of classical phonology and a master of ancient prose, wrote no article but sent Chen and Hu long letters of small criticisms and great praise, also printed in New Youth; that so eminent a classicist should sympathize buoyed their cause. Zhao Yuanren, Hu's fellow student at Cornell and his partner in the earlier pair of papers, often said, in our translation, that Hu's vernacular poems and essays were not vernacular enough, not the genuine spoken style ordinary people used. Hu admitted it. He compared himself to a woman who had bound her feet for forty, or even twenty, years: however much she loosened the bindings, she would never recover natural feet.

paras.zh: 胡适自己对来龙去脉的解释是反对单因论。他开玩笑说，历史上的意外事件往往比“单因”（经济、色欲、上帝之类）更重要：正因为这些单因对所有事件皆可解释，它们也就不可解释任何事件。就他这段经历而言，他明确把送别诗称作「意外的小事」，并说「一连串的小意外事件，逐渐地强迫我采取了这个立场」。他也把湖上险事称作「小小的意外事件」，说它「引起了连锁性的反应」。本文把那张传单也放进这一串，这是本文的归并。把一连串小意外看作推力，是他本人的史观，不是本文的结论。
paras.en: Hu's own explanation of how it all happened is that he opposed single-cause theories of history. He used to joke that accidents often matter more than any monistic cause, such as economics, lust or God: those single causes explain everything that has ever happened, and precisely because they explain everything, they explain nothing. In this episode he explicitly called the farewell poem a small accident, and said that a chain of small accidents had gradually forced him into his position. Hu himself also called the Cayuga Lake incident a small accident that set off a chain reaction. Adding the leaflet to that chain is this article's own grouping. Reading a chain of small accidents as the push behind his position is Hu's own view of history, not a finding of this article.

paras.zh: 作者推断：他选择以身作则，并不只是姿态，而是把分歧改造成可检验的问题。“白话不能用之于诗”是个全称判断，理论上一首像样的白话诗就能动摇它；反之，没有诗，再多书信也只是意见相持。他把新诗集提前定名《尝试集》，等于先给自己揽下举证责任，把胜负交给一场公开、长期、别人看得见的试验。一种解释是，这也呼应了译注者唐德刚对他的定位——夹在必然与偶然之间的“实验主义者”，不肯听任事情自然演变，而要在试验中寻找方向。不过「没有“胡适”，恐怕也就没有“白话文运动”——至少运动也不会在那时就发生了」是唐德刚的评论，不是可核实的史实。
paras.en: The author's inference: his decision to lead by example was not merely a pose; it converted a disagreement into a testable question. The claim that the vernacular cannot be used for poetry is a universal one, and one decent vernacular poem is enough in principle to shake it; without a poem, letters could go on forever as a standoff of opinions. By naming the collection Experiments in advance, he took on the burden of proof in advance and left the outcome to a long, open trial that others could watch. One reading is that this matches the translator-editor Tang Degang's portrait of him as a pragmatist standing between necessity and chance, unwilling to let events drift and determined to search out the right direction through experiment. Still, Tang's remark — in paraphrase, that without Hu Shi there would probably have been no Vernacular Movement, or at least it would not have happened then — is commentary, not verifiable history.

paras.zh: 另一种解释是关于措辞的分工：他把“革命”换成“改良”，把结论降格为“刍议”，自己承担温和的发表风险；陈独秀随后把它高举为“文学革命”，由更激进的人去举旗。据胡适转述，陈独秀坦白说首举义旗的是胡适，他自己高张大旗作声援。这种“一人放低、一人举高”的配合，是作者从先后次序读出的一种可能，属本文的推断。
paras.en: A second reading concerns the division of labour over words. He swapped revolution for reform and demoted his conclusion to a humble opinion, taking on himself the risk of publishing moderately; Chen Duxiu then raised it as literary revolution, and a more radical man carried the flag. By Hu's report, Chen said frankly that the banner was Hu's and that he himself was raising it high in support. This doubling — one man lowering the volume, one raising it — is a possibility the author reads in the sequence; it is this article's inference.

paras.zh: 结局也可以交代一笔。胡适自述，运动约四年就在学校教育上基本成功：1920年北京政府教育部通令，国民小学一、二年级教材一律改用白话，旧教材分期废除。他说这场斗争“至少获得了部分的胜利”，其中重要的部分是以白话为教育工具。他同时说，1919年的学生运动把文化运动变成了政治运动，对文艺复兴运动是一种“干扰”，虽则对传播白话文功不可没。但他也说自己「还是感觉到不满意」：四十年来白话文始终没有成为完全的教育工具和文学工具。他把主要原因归于执政者的保守，以及文白夹杂的教科书。这是他本人的判断。
paras.en: The outcome can be set down too. By Hu's account, in only about four years the effort to replace the classical language with the vernacular in the schools had all but succeeded: in 1920 the Ministry of Education of the Beijing government ordered that all first- and second-year textbooks in the national primary schools be written entirely in the vernacular, with the old textbooks abolished in stages. He said the struggle had won at least a partial victory, the important part being the vernacular as the instrument of education. He also said the student movement of 1919 had been an interruption to the Renaissance movement, turning a cultural movement into a political one, though it did much to spread the vernacular. Yet he said he still felt dissatisfied: in forty years the vernacular had never become a complete instrument of education and literature. He blamed this chiefly on the conservatism of those in power and on textbooks that mixed the classical and the vernacular. This is his own judgment.

paras.zh: 设想你在一支十来人的产品团队里，想把每周汇报从长文档改成几行要点，一位资深同事坚持“正式文档必须写全”。争吵两个月，谁也没动。可以借的是胡适的顺序：先弄清对方真正不让步的是哪一处——通常只剩一处，比如对外的那一节——把争论收缩到这个点，再做一个短小、公开的试验：同一份内容两种写法各出一版，让真正读它的人选，并事先说定看什么指标。试验要能被双方看见，否则又回到各说各话。
paras.en: Suppose you are on a product team of ten or twelve and want to turn the weekly report from a long document into a few bullet points. A senior colleague insists the formal document must be written out in full. Two months of argument, and nobody has moved. What you can borrow from Hu is the order of operations. First find the one place the other side will not give up — there is usually only one, perhaps the section that goes to customers — and shrink the dispute to that point. Then run a small, public experiment: produce two versions of the same content in the two formats, let the people who actually read it choose, and agree beforehand on what counts as evidence. The trial has to be visible to both sides, or the argument slides back into two monologues.

paras.zh: 第二件事是措辞。你把方案叫做“优化”，心里想的是换掉整套流程；这时有人替你把它命名为“流程革命”，还抄送了全员。要不要接？胡适自己的文章用了温和的词，后来是陈独秀把它举成“革命”。接住响亮说法的好处是声量大，代价是解释权易手，而被温和措辞吸引来的中间派，可能被激进的命名吓退。这是作者提出的取舍，并非只有这一种做法。
paras.en: The second thing is wording. You call your plan an optimization while meaning to replace the whole process; someone else renames it a process revolution and copies the whole company. Do you accept the label? Hu's own article used moderate words; it was Chen Duxiu who later raised it as a revolution. Taking the ringing phrase buys attention; the cost is losing control of the definition, and the middle-of-the-road people drawn in by gentle wording may be scared off by a radical name. This is the trade-off the author offers; it is not the only way.

paras.zh: 本文材料只来自一本书：胡适口述、唐德刚译注《胡适口述自传》（中国文史出版社2020年）。按唐德刚说明，这一章英文稿是从《四十自述》中《逼上梁山》那一章节译、经胡适手订后又回译成中文的，与原文多少有点出入。因此这是当事人多年后的自述，不是当时的独立记录；梅光迪、任鸿隽的反应和话语，都经胡适转述，本文不推测他们的内心。
paras.en: The material here comes from one book only: Hu Shi's oral memoir, translated and annotated by Tang Degang, The Oral Memoir of Hu Shi (Chinese Literature and History Press, 2020). As Tang explains, the English draft of this chapter was abridged from the Bi shang Liangshan (Driven to Liangshan) chapter of Hu's Forty Self-Narratives, revised in Hu's own hand, then translated back into Chinese — and it differs from the original in some degree. This is therefore a participant's account given many years later, not an independent record from the time. Mei Guangdi's and Ren Hongjun's reactions and their words all reach us through Hu's retelling, and this piece does not speculate about their inner thoughts.

paras.zh: 他为何用“改良”不用“革命”，是本人事后的解释。唐德刚的说法则是译注者的评论：他认为“文言是半死的文字”这句口号当年有摧枯拉朽的功能，但真实性值得重新商榷；他又认为白话文是百分之百成功，白话诗则未必，至少还未脱离“尝试”阶段。
paras.en: Why he used reform rather than revolution is his own retrospective explanation. Tang Degang's remarks are the annotator's commentary: he thought the slogan that the classical language is a half-dead form of writing had a devastating force in its day, but that its truth is worth debating again; and he judged vernacular prose a hundred per cent successful, while vernacular poetry was not necessarily so, and at least had not yet left the experimental stage.

paras.zh: 唐德刚也记下，反对胡适的人觉得他居功太多；1956年胡适在哈佛大学以这一论调讲演时，后来为他作传的格里德简直嗤之以鼻。
paras.en: Tang also records that Hu's opponents felt he claimed too much credit; when Hu gave this account in a 1956 lecture at Harvard, Jerome B. Grieder, later his biographer, simply scoffed at it.

scenario.zh: 作者提出的现代虚构场景：一位在公司做设计的年轻人想让父母相信，转行做独立设计也能养活自己。父母的回应是“这行不稳定，别人能成是别人的事”。
scenario.en: A fictional scenario offered by the author: a young designer at a company wants to convince their parents that going independent as a designer would pay the bills. The parents' answer is that the field is unstable, and other people's success is other people's business.

question.zh: 当对方承认一件事在别的领域可行、唯独在你这行不行时，是继续举别人的成功例子，还是先做一个能被双方看见的小试验？如果做试验，什么才够格当判断标准？
question.en: When the other side admits that something works everywhere except in your line of work, do you keep piling up other people's success stories, or do you first run a small experiment both sides can watch? And if you run one, what should count as the criterion of judgment?

assumptions.zh:
父母真正担心的是收入不稳定，不是设计这一行本身
三到六个月内，有可能接到可展示、有收入记录的委托
双方愿意用公开可查的结果做判断依据，而不是每通电话都辩论
assumptions.en: The parents' real worry is unstable income, not design as a field. Within three to six months it is possible to win commissions that can be shown and recorded as income. Both sides are willing to judge on publicly checkable results instead of relitigating on every phone call.

steps.zh:
把争论收缩到一个点：能否持续接到付费委托，而不是“这个行业好不好”
用业余时间做小规模尝试，把委托、收入、被拒的稿子都记在同一张表上
事先约定判断标准和期限，到点一起看记录再决定加码还是收手
steps.en: First, shrink the argument to one point: whether paid commissions can be won consistently, not whether the industry is any good. Second, try it on the side and keep one sheet recording commissions, income and rejected drafts. Third, agree in advance on the criteria and the deadline; when the date arrives, look at the record together and decide whether to scale up or stop.

alternative.zh: 作者提出的替代选择：不做试验，改找更多同行成功的故事去说服，代价是对方总可以说“那是别人”，争论不会收敛；或者干脆辞职全力投入，代价是把一次性成败当唯一证据，失败了也没有退路。
alternative.en: An alternative the author suggests: skip the experiment and collect more stories of successful peers instead — the cost is that the other side can always say that is someone else, and the argument never converges. Or quit and go all in at once, where the cost is treating a single shot at success as the only evidence, with nothing to fall back on if it fails.

uncertainty_note.zh: 本文只有胡适晚年口述一种来源，且经节译、手订与回译。梅光迪、任鸿隽的言行均为胡适转述，胡适对动机的说明是事后自述。唐德刚注释中的评价与推论属评论；注中所记之事（如1956年胡适在哈佛讲演时格里德的反应）是唐德刚的记述，本文未另行核验。凡标为 interpretation 的段落是作者推断，标为 modern 的段落是为今日读者虚构的场景。
uncertainty_note.en: This piece rests on a single source: Hu Shi's oral memoir in later life, itself abridged, revised in his own hand and translated back. Mei Guangdi's and Ren Hongjun's words and deeds reach us only through Hu's retelling, and Hu's explanations of motive are retrospective. Tang Degang's evaluations and inferences are commentary; the events he records (such as Grieder's reaction to Hu's 1956 Harvard lecture) are his testimony, not checked here. Paragraphs marked interpretation are the author's inferences, and paragraphs marked modern are scenarios invented for readers today.

preheader.zh: 朋友们让步到只剩“诗”这一处，他没有再争，而是决定自己去试
preheader.en: When his friends conceded everything but poetry, he stopped arguing and decided to run the experiment himself
